title: Parent Communication Apps, Rated
author: RatedEd
summary: RatedEd's teacher-facing review rates the major parent-communication platforms -- TalkingPoints, Remind Chat, ParentSquare, ClassDojo, Bloomz, plus a warning on Seesaw and ClassTag -- on one criterion that most marketing ignores: whether the tool actually reaches families, not just whether it advertises translation. The reviewer's key insight is that message translation and interface translation are different capabilities, and most platforms handle the first well while leaving menus, buttons, and permission workflows in English, undermining the feature for families who can't navigate the app itself. TalkingPoints and Remind Chat earn the top individual-teacher picks for building around genuine reach, while ParentSquare is rated highly only at the district level given its cost and scale. The piece also flags a landscape shift that caught many teachers off guard: Remind was quietly absorbed into ParentSquare, Seesaw dropped individual teacher licenses entirely, and ClassTag's free tier sunset into a district-only product. It closes with practical advice for protecting teacher time, since the app itself never sets the boundary; the first three weeks of a teacher's own reply habits do.
points: The rating's central distinction is message translation versus interface translation: most parent-communication apps translate the text of a notification but leave menus, buttons, and permission workflows in English.
TalkingPoints and Remind Chat top the individual-teacher picks because they're free and built around actual family reach, rather than platform features.
Two once-popular teacher tools quietly closed off to individual educators: Seesaw now requires a school/district purchase, and ClassTag's free tier sunset into the district-only SchoolStatus Connect.

The piece's practical framing extends past app selection to teacher self-protection: publish a stated response window and turn off after-hours push notifications, because a 10pm reply trains families to expect 10pm replies.
quotes: A parent who cannot read the navigation, the notification, or the permission slip does not benefit much from a beautifully translated announcement sitting behind three English menus. It is the difference between a feature and an outcome, and almost nobody tests for it.
ParentSquare acquired Remind in 2023, and Hub customers have been moved toward ParentSquare since. Remind still exists as a light teacher tool. It is no longer an independent path for a district.

Built specifically around two-way multilingual messaging. Translation is the product rather than a feature someone added in a later release, and it consistently rates highest in the category for multilingual reach.

Translating the text of a message is not the same as translating the app. Buttons, menus, navigation, and permission workflows frequently stay in English. Ask to see the parent-side experience in Spanish before you sign anything.
Delivery beats interface. The prettiest app your families have not downloaded reaches nobody. Plain SMS is unglamorous and it works.
Duplication costs you. If your district bought a platform, adding a parallel system means families check two places and you maintain two systems.
